methodology: Compared Qur'an 4:92 Arabic and English with Numbers 35 and Deuteronomy 19 English ESV; considered Exodus 22 and Leviticus 19 English ESV for migrant motifs. Other verses given verse-specific first-pass classifications. No Hebrew critical editions or manuscripts collated; no dependence claims.

verses.summary: Conflict with groups who seek safety from both sides but return to hostility; conditional combat directive
Accidental killing: manumission, compensation, treaty categories, and fasting alternative
Deliberate killing of a believer and eschatological punishment
Verification before treating a person as an enemy; warning against rejecting a greeting or profession of peace
Those who remain at home contrasted with those who strive, with an exception for disability
Different degrees of reward for striving and those who remain
Angelic rebuke of those who failed to migrate despite capacity; divine earth described as spacious
Exception for vulnerable men, women, and children unable to migrate
Hope of pardon for those genuinely unable to migrate
Migration for God's cause, places of refuge and provision, and death during migration

staged_candidates.similarity: Intentional and unintentional killing receive different legal treatment.
staged_candidates.difference: Numbers/Deuteronomy emphasize refuge cities, blood avenger and adjudication; Qur'an 4:92 prescribes freeing a believing enslaved person, family compensation differentiated by political relation, and a two-month fast when unable.
staged_candidates.verification: English ESV passage checked; Qur'anic Arabic and English 4:92 checked. No Hebrew critical apparatus, LXX collation or manuscript dating verified; staged only.
